A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we develop a novel self-adaptive 3D human-pose estimation framework, which only requires a single unlabeled target domain image to adapt a source trained regressor.

, in contrast to existing works that require a 2D pose annotation in the target domain to perform domain-adaptation, our method is the first to perform unsupervised domain adaptation in the 3D pose space using only a silhouette annotation.
we are proposing an end-to-end self-adaptive 3D human-pose estimation framework that relies only upon silhouette supervision to train the model on a source domain and adapt it to a target domain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, a model trained on synthetic data with only silhouette supervision can generalize well on real data with only silhouette labels.

the proposed spatial topological alignment loss can effectively align the silhouette topology of a target image to that of a source image, and thus enable a source-trained regressor to generalize well to the target domain.
, in the absence (or in conjunction) of any 2D pose supervision, the topology-centric Chamfer loss is a strong and reliable cue for 3D pose recovery.
